fatal_errors: The proposed surface-nanostructuring intervention is absent from the target study, which investigates temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction of the unchanged coating.
The stated temperature, velocity, and wear-depth limits are invented and conflict with the target conditions of 300–1200 K, 10 m/s indentation, and 30 Å depth.
The mechanism based on increased roughness and hardness does not reproduce the observed transition from dislocation and stacking-fault deformation to lattice disorder above approximately 900 K.
The cited evidence concerns a different CoCrFeMnNbNi coating and does not report or support surface nanostructuring as a wear-resistance intervention.
Post-wear SEM cannot by itself resolve the atomic-scale, dynamically evolving HCP fraction, stacking faults, lattice disorder, or dislocation-line density required to test the target mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the FeNiCrCoCu-on-Cu wear problem and supplies an unchanged-coating comparator, but otherwise has little scientific agreement with the target. It misses the controlled-temperature nanoindentation/friction protocol, the approximately 900 K degradation threshold, the nonmonotonic elastic modulus, the sharp hardness decline, and increased friction fluctuations at high temperature. Its boundaries lack evidentiary support and are on incompatible length and temperature scales. A discriminating test would compare otherwise identical simulations or experiments at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K while tracking HCP atom fraction, lattice disorder, dislocation-line length, hardness/modulus, tangential force, and friction coefficient during indentation and sliding.
